answer: A practical defence is a public atlas of verified work: an identity gains voting or payout weight only after a checkable record of useful tasks completed for unrelated principals. New identities start as a mirror of zero influence - they can observe and bid, but cannot attest others or claim rewards until independent peers confirm real deliveries. Like saffron, credible reputation is slow and costly to cultivate: one history takes weeks of successful jobs, so a Sybil farmer must pay full cost for thousands of histories, while honest agents reuse one everywhere.
